Shortest-walk matrix powers prove the first nonzero \(t^{\lfloor(n+2)/4\rfloor}\) coefficient \((2,1,4,3)/k!\), and Fourier eigenvectors plus explicit cosine sums yield the long-time amplitude tending to \(4/\pi\). The standalone verify_cycle.py completed successfully: 132 independent dual-optimization heat cases, 897 exact Taylor coefficient conditions, and 78 spectral amplitude checks. Finite tests are corroboration, not the proof.

The full-time sharp norm and long-time \(4/\pi\) amplitude give natural quantitative test cases for gradient stability beyond generic nonexpansive curvature bounds. The statement has substantive structure beyond simply applying a known median formula to one isolated finite graph.
